title: The Devil In The White City

questions.q: What was Chicago like at the end of the 1800s, according to the summary?
a: Violent and unsanitary, with police unable to keep up
Peaceful and prosperous, with little crime
Small and rural, with few industries
Well policed but short of housing
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes daily murders, disease-ridden water, trash-filled streets and an understaffed police force.

questions.q: Why did the United States want to host its own world's fair?
a: To repair its cultural reputation after a poor showing in Paris
To celebrate the end of a long economic depression
To show Europe that it had won a recent war
To raise money for Chicago's struggling police force
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that after an embarrassing display at France's fair, the US wanted to prove its cultural standing.

questions.q: What problems did Burnham face while preparing the fair?
a: A recession, labor unrest, quarreling officials and bad weather
A shortage of architects and a lack of land
Flooding that destroyed the fairgrounds
A boycott by foreign exhibitors
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists those obstacles and notes that the fair still opened on time in 1893.

questions.q: Which attractions debuted at the World's Columbian Exposition?
a: The Ferris Wheel, the zipper and an all-electric kitchen
The telephone, the airplane and the radio
The escalator, the typewriter and the telegraph
The automobile, the phonograph and the camera
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists the first Ferris Wheel, the zipper and an electric kitchen among the fair's innovations.

questions.q: How did Holmes use the fair to reach his victims?
a: He ran a hotel that appealed to visiting fairgoers
He worked as a guard at the fair's entrance
He sold tickets to a fake exhibit
He posed as a doctor treating fair workers
questions.why: Lesson 3 says his charming hotel, close to the fair, drew guests into a building rigged as a death trap.
